news.title: Americans trust science more than peers around the world, survey shows
news.summary: Just 40 percent of Americans reported a lot of confidence in U.S. hospitals and health clinics, the same proportion as in Portugal and Uruguay.

news.title: Rep. Pallone introduces bill replacing No Surprises Act's arbitration process
news.summary: One of the No Surprises Act’s chief authors wants to replace the "broken" system for settling out-of-network pay disputes with market-based benchmarks.

news.title: Oracle Health data breach in 2025 compromised data of 20M people: report
news.summary: In a report issued October 2, the Texas attorney general said the company disclosed that Social Security numbers, addresses and medical information of almost 20 million people, including about 3 million Texans, Bloomberg reported.

news.title: Industry Voices—Why health system CFOs can't budget their way out of coverage disruption
news.summary: Semi-annual redeterminations and work requirements will test payer-mix assumptions across the industry over the next two years. Now is the time for health systems to prepare, writes Ensemble SVP Matthew Ennen.

news.title: Fierce Healthcare Regulatory Recap: CMS releases 2027 MA star ratings; HHS awards $28M for falls prevention
news.summary: The latest news from CMS, HHS and more across Washington, D.C.

news.summary: The latest news from Nextech, Assort Health, EliseAI, Elsevier, Arcadia, Solera Health and more.

news.title: Humana rebounds, Aetna slips: Winners and losers in the 2027 MA star ratings
news.summary: Federal regulators released the hotly anticipated star ratings for the 2027 Medicare Advantage plan year, and winners and losers emerged in the data.

news.title: Abridge, University of Texas System enter enterprise-wide agreement for expanded AI-enabled care
news.summary: The partnership establishes a systemwide framework for the eight UT health institutions to access Abridge.

news.title: Hospital industry sues to block HHS' 340B rebate pilot (again)
news.summary: The American Hospital Association and others have launched a legal rematch with the federal government over the second iteration of a pilot program swapping out safety-net hospitals’ upfront drug discounts for after-the-fact rebates.

news.title: Urban hospitals face closure rates similar to rural facilities, study finds
news.summary: There were 432 acute hospital closures and 216 openings across the country from 2010 through 2025, with the former accelerating over time and the latter slowing, according to a new study. Closure rates were statistically similar between rural and urban hospitals, and generally increased among safety net facilities and for-profits.

news.title: Little room for stakeholder consensus among potential Medicare Advantage reforms
news.summary: A survey of 52 experts spanning researchers, the Medicare Advantage industry, patient advocates and policymakers wasn't able to identify a single policy proposal that would be received wholeheartedly by all three groups.

news.title: CMS: About 71% of MAPD plan enrollees in coverage with four or more stars for 2027
news.summary: The Trump administration has released the 2027 Medicare Advantage star ratings, with many enrollees in plans that earned at least four stars.

news.title: HHS launches 4 new vaccine injury research, reporting initiatives
news.summary: The U.S. Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) on Thursday announced a series of actions aimed at strengthening the federal government's response to vaccine-related health concerns.

news.title: Parkinson’s-focused Aspen and bispecific biotech Bambusa plan IPOs
news.summary: Parkinson’s disease cell therapy-focused Aspen Neuroscience and bispecific biotech Bambusa Therapeutics are the latest drug developers to eye up a public listing.

news.title: Ferass Abuzaina named Worldwide President of Surgery at BD

news.title: GSK drinks in Chai Discovery’s AI models after wet-lab validation
news.summary: GSK has joined Chai Discovery’s growing roster of Big Pharma clients, signing up to access protein-folding and design models.

news.title: ‘We’re making a lot of progress’: How Nobel-winning optogenetics is being harnessed by biotechs
news.summary: As a notorious night owl, it was already very early in the morning of October 5 when Karl Deisseroth, M.D., Ph.D., finally laid down to get some shuteye. Not long after, the phone of the Stanford psychiatrist and bioengineer lit up with an incoming call from Sweden.

news.title: Chutes & Ladders—Vir looks to Liu to lead late-stage push
news.summary: As Vir pushes its lead hepatitis D combo through phase 3 development, the biotech has tapped an experienced medical expert to light the way. David Liu, M.D., Ph.D., is now Vir’s chief medical officer, after most recently serving in the same role at Nuvation Bio.

news.title: How we picked the Fierce 15
news.summary: What does it mean to be a Fierce 15 biotech in 2026? With this year’s list unveiled, the Fierce Biotech team gets together to discuss what the winners tell us about the state of the sector.

news.title: Lilly-backed TRex rakes in $117M IPO, while hypertension biotech Retension reveals $45M listing
news.summary: Eli Lilly-backed TRex Bio and hypertension-focused Retension Pharmaceuticals brought in $116.7 million and $45 million from their respective IPOs, continuing a bumper year for biotech listings.

news.title: Endeavor’s threat to IPF incumbents increases after phase 2 win for Hedgehog inhibitor
news.summary: Endeavor BioMedicines solidified its potential threat to Big Pharma with a phase 2b readout suggesting its Hedgehog inhibitor could become the first drug to reduce lung fibrosis while increasing total lung capacity.

news.title: AI biotech Iambic aims for $135M IPO to push cancer drugs through clinic
news.summary: Iambic Therapeutics is aiming to raise $135 million in net proceeds from an IPO as the AI biotech looks to fund the clinical development of its lead cancer drug.

news.title: ‘It’s just survival now’: Why is almost a third of Boston’s life sciences lab space sitting vacant?
news.summary: Vacancy rates for lab and manufacturing spaces in Massachusetts increased 11-fold to 31% between 2021 and 2026. So what's gone wrong?

news.title: Ono pays $80M for regional rights to trio of Biohaven IgG degraders, including phase 3 Grave’s asset
news.summary: Japan’s Ono Pharmaceutical is paying $80 million upfront for the regional rights to a trio of Biohaven’s IgG degraders, led by a phase 3-stage Grave’s disease prospect.

news.title: Zealand, Roche’s ‘intriguing’ weight loss for amylin drug soured by blood sugar data
news.summary: Zealand Pharma has reported more phase 2 data on its Roche-partnered amylin analog, linking the drug candidate to competitive weight loss but a lackluster effect on blood sugar.

papers.summary: Biological reasoning models use post-training to connect LLMs to biological foundation model representations and biological text. papers.title: From Given to Gathered Evidence: Agentic Learning for Longitudinal Medical Reasoning
papers.summary: Foundation models can serve as clinical agents through tool-use harnesses. However, conventional medical benchmarks assess reasoning over preselected evidence rather than the ability to seek it across clinical records and longitudinal imaging. We propose CASE: a series of role-specific Clinical Agents for Seeking Evidence, together with a tool-use harness and an agentic post-training framework for compact vision-language policy models. papers.title: GraphDecisionBench: Benchmarking System One Models on Graph Tasks
papers.summary: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly explored for graph understanding and decision-making, while System One models such as Jev select directly from supplied options. However, the capabilities of System One models on graph-related tasks remain unclear. We introduce GraphDecide, a model-independent benchmark that combines structural task profiles, matched graph-text input contrasts and heuristic-proposal controls to diagnose graph decision performance. papers.title: AMLworld-Compact: Importance-Weighted Downsampling for Cost-Effective LLM Evaluation and Error Diagnosis
papers.summary: Evaluating large language models (LLMs) on AMLworld's smallest test splits is costly because each of over a million targets requires a separate graph prompt. Sampling reduces this cost, but small balanced subsets change unweighted precision and F1. We introduce AMLworld-Compact, an evaluation set that retains every illicit test transaction and samples benign transactions from supervised-score strata. papers.title: Opera: A Verbal Critic Framework for Long-horizon Coding Agents
papers.summary: Long-horizon coding agents need timely corrections, yet feedback can be ineffective or even harmful when it misjudges ongoing work or fails to address the underlying problem. Existing critics focus on evaluating trajectories and generating feedback, but rarely track what happens after feedback is delivered. We present Opera, a verbal critic framework that treats each correction as a persistent note, followed until the diagnosed problem is resolved. papers.title: Incidental information contaminates patient notes and disrupts clinical reasoning in large language models
papers.summary: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly relied upon to support ambient documentation and clinical reasoning. Here we examine the impact of a failure mode shared between these two applications by assessing their sensitivity to information incidental to the patient encounter. In 576 patient-clinician dialogues, we found that frontier models inserted small-talk exchanges into 35% of notes, while mean quality scores changed by at most 0.20 points on five-point scales. papers.title: Frozen Models, Evolving Expertise: Model-Agnostic Learning from Deployment Experience for Multimodal Medical AI
papers.summary: Large language models (LLMs) and vision-language models (VLMs) are usually frozen after deployment, so they do not learn from the cases they solve. This is especially concerning in medicine, where new clinical evidence, updated guidelines, and new therapies can change established practice. Fine-tuning can update the model, but it requires access to model weights and additional training.
